channel.title: Wisconsin Newspaper Association - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Newspaper Association (wnanews.com)

item.title: Reporters: Apply now for six new environmental reporting positions with the Ag & Water Desk
item.description: The Mississippi River Basin Ag & Water Desk, an environmental news network covering America's largest watershed, is seeking talented journalists to join six newsrooms through Report for America's 2026 class. The application deadline is Feb. 16, 2026.

item.title: Pulitzer-Prize winning editor joins Gazette as president, publisher
item.description: Adams MultiMedia, the parent company of The Gazette, announced Jan. 27 that Richard Green, a longtime media executive and editor, will be regional president and publisher of The Cedar Rapids Gazette and 11 other community newspaper titles in Iowa.

item.title: Wisconsin’s state and local tax burden remains at record low
item.description: Wisconsin’s tax burden remained at an all-time low in 2025, as its residents’ combined incomes grew at the same rate as state and local tax collections.

item.title: Dane County District Attorney: No evidence that Village of Blue Mounds violated open meetings law
item.description: Both the Blue Mounds village attorney and Dane County District Attorney Ishmael Ozanne have found the village followed proper protocols and did not violate any open meetings laws in October 2025 despite accusations from the former village president.

item.title: Walker rejects Melms’ $50K demand, stands by reporting
item.description: Lakeland Times and Northwoods River News publisher and WNA Foundation board member Gregg Walker this week rejected a demand for a $50,000 payment to attorney Frederick Melms and said he will not withdraw a professional misconduct complaint against the attorney or retract the newspaper’s reporting after Melms threatened a defamation lawsuit.

item.title: Legislation, local approvals uncertain, but experts say data center projects could lead to energy innovation
item.description: As communities and companies navigate the path ahead for mega data centers in Wisconsin, some say the massive building projects could lead to expansion of renewable energy, a stronger grid and new energy technologies.

item.title: National Weddings Month: Wisconsin’s top 3 counties for dream weddings
item.description: National Weddings Month is here, and with it comes the excitement of choosing where your love story will unfold in Wisconsin.

item.title: Business coverage vital to your product and community
item.description: Editors are regularly solicited to publish news that puts merchants in good standing. Here are some suggestions to consider when handling business news.

item.title: A FOIA fight over immigration records
item.description: Our country’s current fight over immigration enforcement is also a fight over government transparency.

item.title: Congressional candidate settled $44M lawsuit tied to Ponzi scheme
item.description: A Republican congressional candidate emphasizing his deep roots in northern Wisconsin settled a federal lawsuit for $44 million while based in California, court records show.
